title: Evading IDS, Firewalls, and Honeypots

objectives.text: Distinguish IDS from IPS and name the three detection methodologies (signature, anomaly, stateful protocol analysis) with one strength and one weakness of each
Classify an IDPS as network-based, host-based, wireless or NBA, and tell inline from passive deployment from a scenario
Match a firewall type (packet filter, stateful, proxy/application, circuit-level, NGFW, UTM, WAF) to what it inspects, and place a DMZ, bastion host and NAT in a network layout
Read a Snort or Suricata rule: identify the action, header, direction operator and key options (msg, sid, rev, classtype, content, flow)
Classify honeypots by interaction level and purpose, distinguish honeynet types and honeytokens, and explain why honeypot alerts have few false positives
Select perimeter and sensor controls: deny-by-default, ingress/egress filtering, traffic normalization and target-based reassembly, TLS inspection, layered detection and segmentation

readingMap.why: The detection methodologies, IDS-vs-IPS response, IDPS types and inline-vs-passive are tested directly and underpin the rest of the module.
Firewall types, DMZ/bastion/NAT and reading a Snort or Suricata rule are frequent recall and command-output questions.

labs.name: Write and test Snort 3 rules against a sample pcap
labs.skill: Building a rule header and options (msg, sid, content, flow) and confirming it alerts on the intended traffic

labs.name: Run Suricata on a captured pcap and read the eve.json alerts
labs.skill: Replaying traffic through Suricata and interpreting alert, flow and http records in EVE JSON

labs.name: Deploy a low-interaction honeypot (Cowrie) in an isolated VM and review the captured session log
labs.skill: Standing up an SSH/Telnet decoy and reading the attacker's commands, with no production system attached

labs.name: Create a canary token and observe the alert when it is triggered
labs.skill: Placing a decoy credential/file/URL as a high-signal tripwire and confirming the alert fires on use

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a colleague the difference between signature-based and anomaly-based detection, and why each one misses a different kind of attack.
Explain why a network IDS must reassemble traffic the same way the destination host does, and what Snort frag3 or Suricata host-os-policy do to achieve that.
Explain why a honeypot's alerts have very few false positives, and what a defender does to keep a decoy credible.
